text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Neck (likely from head and neck primary) with a history of colon cancer.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a progressive, painless, cystic neck mass for two months. While the ultrasound suggests a cystic nature, the history of colon cancer and current diabetes requires ruling out metastatic disease or an infected epidermoid cyst (sebaceous cyst), particularly given the potential for secondary infection or malignancy in a diabetic patient. The absence of fever or pain makes an acute abscess less likely, but the progressive nature warrants further investigation into the nature of the cyst.
